text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- 50,000 new telephone lines are to be provided in Ikeja and Apapa business districts of Lagos, where exchanges were destroyed in separate fires. The managing director of Nigerian Telecommunications who made the announcement did not set a specific date.
- Chinese team expected in Nigeria on Thursday to begin talks on possible construction of additional power stations.
- Nigeria's 36 states will this month share grants from central government totalling 17.4 billion naira.

- Leadership tussles in Ogoniland, home of executed activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, may have stalled a 3.12 billion naira four-year plan by Shell Petroleum Development Company to restart oil production in the area. Shell pulled out in 1993 after acts of sabotage by Ogonis.
- Diplomatic row between Nigeria and Canada is holding up installation of a computerised Central Securities Clearing System at the Nigerian stock exchnage.
- Federal government orders all casinos to register their businesses with the ministry of commerce and tourism to forestall money laundering.
